title: Consumption Responses to an Unpopular Policy: Evidence from a Short-Lived Soda Tax
eligible_reason: Single-policy design. The treatment is the Washington State soda tax during its short life in 2010 (isWA x is_tax_month, one state, one tax window, switched off by the November 2010 referendum). Specifications are felm regressions of UPC-store-week volume/price on isWA:is_tax_month plus its interaction with zip-code referendum vote share (Doverturn6), with upc_store_moy and upc_chain_month FE, and IV versions instrumenting the vote-share interaction with Republican vote shares (repfracGov, repfracUSH). Augmented versions add income-quartile x tax-month terms. Generalized synthetic control (gsynth) is used as a robustness check. No unit-specific adoption dates; the main effect of interest is a triple-difference heterogeneity term and an IV estimate.
design_notes: R (lfe::felm, gsynth). Pipeline: 2_store_level_variables.R, 3a_soda_scanner_merging.R, 3b_create_price_instruments.R, 3c_final_data_create.R, then fairness_analysis_replication_file.R (main), fairness_analysis_alt_shopping_trips.R (HMS appendix), fairness_analysis_oregon.R (Appendix F, Oregon as alternative control). rhs_base_noiv = 'isWA:is_tax_month + isWA:is_tax_month:Doverturn6 | upc_store_moy + upc_chain_month | 0 | upc_store + store_month'.
data_provenance_note: NielsenIQ RMS (2009-2012) and HMS (2004-2016) scanner data must be obtained from Kilts; only auxiliary vote, weather, DMA and centroid files are shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). One treated state and one tax window; not a staggered design.
